data.body:
CORRECTION to the ruling recorded above (2026-08-07). My previous comment overstated it as a blanket rejection of any N/A vocabulary. That is wrong, and the ticket is reopened.

The refined ruling distinguishes by CLOSE DISPOSITION:

**Closing as COMPLETED — no N/A.** Every acceptance criterion must be met, or the criterion is itself defective and must be REMEDIATED (rewritten to state what is actually verifiable) before close. An unmeetable AC on a ticket claiming completion is a signal the plan was written wrong, and surfacing it at close time is the gate working. An N/A marker here would convert that signal into a checkbox.

**Closing as WON'T FIX / obsolete / not-a-bug — N/A is GENUINE.** The criteria describe work deliberately NOT being done. They are not defective, and rewriting them is theatre: you would be editing a description to describe work nobody will do, purely to satisfy a checkbox scan. Today the only available answer is --force-close, which is why routine force-closing has become normalised — the gate is asking a question that does not apply.

That distinction is the real defect, and it is implementable rather than vague: the close ALREADY requires an explicit --class for bugs (regression, plan_defect, env_integration, flaky, preexisting, not_a_bug, duplicate, escalated, undetermined). N/A eligibility can key off the class. Terminal-disposition classes (not_a_bug, duplicate, and whatever names won't-fix/obsolete) make the AC scan inapplicable, with the class itself as the recorded reason; completion-shaped closes keep today's strict behaviour unchanged.

Evidence this is a live papercut, from one session on 2026-08-06/07: 3b92 was force-closed as obsolete (its target code was deleted in 381f6bb9d5, so its criteria were unsatisfiable by construction — a textbook genuine N/A); 39c5 and 83f2 were force-closed with criteria that were shipped-but-unmeasurable or blocked on a plan-authoring floor; ed5e was force-closed as a reporting-only defect not worth repairing. Under the refined ruling, at least 3b92 and ed5e should have been clean class-driven closes, not overrides.

The acceptance criteria need rewriting again to match this scope — the ones currently on the ticket record the blanket rejection and are now themselves wrong.
